name: Ōgetsuhime
depicted_variant: The non-graphic crop-origin miracle after death: covered reclining goddess with rice emerging from closed eyes and silkworms from her head.

visual_requirements.description: One reclining adult female deity, one head/two arms/two legs fully covered by opaque robe; closed eyes and no wounds or blood.
Rice plants visibly grow directly from both closed eyes and silkworms emerge through hair at head, literal crop-origin miracle from dead body.

aura: Sacred awe comes from physical crop-origin miracle c05, not glow, living spellcasting or invented giant scale.
artistic_choices: Select rice from eyes and silkworms from head as two explicit details of c05 source quote; other body-origin crops omitted to keep portrayal non-graphic and modest.
Closed fully opaque plain ivory robe, loose dark hair and moonlit dark earthen ground are editorial presentation; no invented crown, emblems, weapons or giant size.
Reclining motionless goddess is deceased c04/c05, while rice actively grows from body; this is a reverent crop-origin moment, never a monstrous attack.
prompt:
ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mitoloka illustration of Ogetsuhime, Japanese food goddess at the moment crops and silkworms miraculously arise from her body after death in the Kojiki.
ANATOMY: ONE adult female goddess with ONE head, TWO CLOSED eyes, TWO arms and TWO legs; she lies reclining diagonally across frame, clearly deceased and completely at rest, hands open, NO wounds or blood. Fully opaque CLOSED plain ivory robe with high neckline, long sleeves and closed ankle-length hem covers her entire body. Loose long black hair around head. [ogetsuhime-c01,ogetsuhime-c04,ogetsuhime-c05]
MOMENT: BURST into living growth from her body: several real rice stalks with ripe drooping grain ears physically emerge DIRECTLY FROM BOTH CLOSED EYES, not from soil behind her and not worn as a crown. White silkworms emerge from among the hair on her head and crawl outward. These two impossible bodily origins MUST be clearly readable, with intact skin and NO injury imagery. Her monumental close head and the vigorous emerging rice are the subject. [ogetsuhime-c05]
POWER: Crop-origin miracle from the deceased goddess, ONLY rice from eyes and silkworms from head selected from documented crop origins. Living rice physically springs upward, stalks cast shadows on her face. No living spellcasting, no resurrection, no aura or other magic effects. [ogetsuhime-c05]
SCALE & CAMERA: very close low side view near shoulder height, head and shoulders occupy half the square; covered body recedes diagonally, both arms visually distinct. Normal human body scale, miracle dominates through close framing rather than invented giant size.
LIGHT & WEATHER: one strong moonlight shaft through deep dark space, bright physical rim on grain ears, face partly shadowed; walnut and ivory palette with muted gold grain.
SURFACE: tactile woven opaque linen, black hair, delicate white silkworms, fibrous rice stalks and heavy real grain ears, dark earth. Strong visible painterly texture.
SETTING: dark unmarked earthen ground, deliberately omit architecture and ritual emblems because the research specifies no setting.
MOOD: sacred, immense awe at life erupting from death; powerful food-origin miracle, respectful, never horror, erotic, decorative flower portrait or ordinary woman sleeping in a field.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: no wounds, decomposition, blood, gore or exposed body; no attack, sword or other deity; no flowers or flower crown; rice must visibly originate at closed eyes, silkworms at head; no generic glow, aura, neon, energy ribbon, text, logo, frame, border, watermark; no extra heads, eyes, arms, legs or fingers; no borrowed film/game/anime designs.
rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.

visual_review.notes: Native1254 and200 inspected: fully covered reclining deceased female goddess c01/c04/c05, one head/two clearly separate arms; lower legs and feet outside the close crop, covered body without visible extra limbs, long sleeves and opaque closed robe. Ripe rice stalks visibly emerge directly from BOTH closed eyes and white silkworms emerge across hair/head, two explicit c05 source details. No blood, wound or exposed body. Physical life-origin miracle dominates face and grain at200, unmistakably supernatural rather than ordinary sleeper; moment is active crop emergence after death, reverent awe rather than monster menace. No aura, invented spellcasting, crown, text or gore. Seven Sangar checks pass for sacred crop-origin depiction.

root_visual_review.notes: Viewed native 1254px, 200px, and face/eye, silkworm/hair and both-hand crops. What works: one adult goddess (ogetsuhime-c01) lying dead (c04) with her eyes closed, no wounds or blood, in a fully opaque ivory robe. Both hands show normal fingers. Rice rises from both closed eyes (c05), one sheaf from the left eye and one from the inner corner of the right, and white silkworms lie in her hair (c05). No Susanoo, aura or text. It fails the sangar test and the tone required for a living religion. (1) The figure is a photographic, ordinary young woman asleep on bare soil in a plain robe, and everything is still: the rice stands motionless, with no sign of growth erupting. At 200px it reads as a sleeping woman with a sheaf of rice over her face, calm rather than awe-inspiring. It fails Uji Sangar #2, #3 and #7 (ordinary woman, calm, static). (2) About a dozen segmented white larvae with dark heads are scattered across her hair and crawl onto the soil away from her head. On a corpse they read as maggots, a sign of decay, not as silkworms being born from her head. For a Kojiki deity of a living Shinto tradition, §6.5 asks for majesty, not the macabre.

correction_notes: Keep: the c05 crop-origin miracle after her death (c04), non-graphic. Closed eyes; no wounds, blood, gore or exposed body; a fully opaque robe; rice from both eyes and silkworms from her head; no Susanoo and no aura. Fix: (a) Make the miracle a powerful event, not a still life. Dense rice stalks surge up out of both eyes in two tall sheaves that rise high above her into the night. Heavy golden ears bend and shed grain that falls like rain onto the dark earth, and the soil around her stirs. Use a low, ground-level camera beside her head so the rice towers over the viewer, with one strong shaft of light on it. Optionally add the other non-graphic c05 origins (millet from the ears, azuki beans from the nose) as small, clear details. (b) Silkworms: a few unmistakable pale silkworm caterpillars emerging at the crown of her head, spinning fine glinting silk with a cocoon or two, so they read as silkworms being born. Not many grubs scattered across her hair and the soil. (c) Paint her in the house painterly style as an ancient Japanese goddess, in ancient-period layered robes (editorial) with serene, dignified features, not a photographic modern young woman. Reverent and majestic, never horror. No text.
